claim: Image-only training of video LLMs yields temporal reasoning performance significantly above chance on benchmarks designed to require temporal understanding, and subsequent video-specific training provides only small improvements.
falsifier: Train a video LLM using only image data (no video data) and evaluate its temporal reasoning on a benchmark that requires temporal understanding; compare performance to a version that additionally undergoes video-specific training. The image-only version should score significantly above chance and the video-trained version should show only small gains.

conditions: Models are trained with a multi-stage procedure where the last stage uses video data
Evaluation is performed on a benchmark (TVBench) designed to require temporal reasoning and not solvable from single frames or text alone
Image-trained versions have never been trained on real videos
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the two Video LLMs trained with the LongVU approach and evaluated on TVBench; transfer to other models, benchmarks, or training procedures is unestablished
